summary: **Parties Present:** Shri Shubham Arya, Advocate, HPPC Ms. Reeha Singh, Advocate, HPPC Ms. Priyansi Jadiya, CTUIL Shri Swapnil Verma, CTUIL Shri Gajendra Singh, NLDC - _(c) Direct Respondents 1 to 5 to take immediate steps to re-compute and render accounting of the loss/charges and give refund to the Petitioner of the amount collected from the Petitioners with interest;_ - _(g) Pass such further order or orders as may be deemed just and proper to give justice to the Petitioners._ - (p) In the meeting of the Validation Committee held on 20.06.2018, wherein the issues raised by HVPNL were discussed, after due deliberations, it was conveyed that the Validation Committee is not the right forum to seek such relief. The Validation Committee advised approaching the Commission on the matter. **3.** The matter was heard on 20.04.2021 through video conferencing. During the course of the hearing, the senior counsel for the Petitioners reiterated the submissions made in the Petition. In response to the Commission's specific query regarding nature of the reliefs sought, the senior counsel submitted that the Petitioners have, inter-alia, sought a declaratory relief under Sections 79(1)(c) and 79(1)(d) of the Act on account of being aggrieved by NLDC's wrong interpretation of the provisions of the 2010 Sharing Regulations and the Commission's order dated 08.06.2013 in Petition No. 44/TL/2012. It was further submitted that the Petitioners are neither contesting the provisions of the 2010 Sharing Regulations nor that the present Petition contains any dispute under the PPAs dated 07.08.2008. After hearing the senior counsel for the Petitioners, the Commission reserved the order on the admissibility of the matter. _9. The issue for our consideration at this stage is whether the present Petition is maintainable in the present form._ **5.** The Commission directed the Petitioner to submit a copy of the PPA with Adani Power (Mundra) Limited, as well as directed the Respondents, including NLDC, to file their reply in the matter. **7.** The Petitioners vide affidavit dated 23.05.2023 have submitted as follows: has not dealt with the specific submissions made by the Petitioners and the Study dated 09.04.2019 conducted by NLDC itself in pursuance of the directions given by the Office of this Commission. - (f) The Petitioners cannot in any manner be considered to be participating in the use of the interstate transmission system from Mundra Thermal Station to Mohindergarh for any purpose, either for consideration for any such marginal value to be applied or otherwise. All such incidences should necessarily be attributed to Adani Power. Accordingly, it is not open to NLDC to involve both Adani Power and the Petitioners in any implication of the said line; and considering Adani Power being responsible and at the same time considering the same line for computation of Petitioner for any charge, i.e., by applying any margin, constitutes charging both the Petitioners and Adani Power. - (i) In terms of the Order dated 24.01.2022 passed by this Commission, as at present and without prejudice to the rights of the Petitioners, are seeking the following: **8.** The Petitioners, vide affidavit dated 24.05.2023, have submitted a copy of the Power Purchase Agreement (‘PPA’) entered into between the Petitioners and Adani Power. - (a) Vide final order dated 18.03.2016 passed in the Petition No. 184/TT/2013, the Commission determined the final tariff and inter alia held that the petitioner has an agreement with Haryana Utilities for 1424 MW and after considering the losses, it will be 1495 MW, and the petitioner will pay the proportionate transmission charges for this capacity. **12.** The Petitioners, vide affidavit dated 07.07.2023, in their common reply, have submitted as follows: **13.** The matter was re-listed for hearing due to a change in the coram. The counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the pleadings in the matter have been completed and that the arguments have also been heard. Learned counsel further submitted that no further oral hearing is required and the Commission may accordingly pass orders. Accordingly, the Commission reserved the order in the matter. **17.** In light of the submissions, the following issues arise for our consideration: **Issue No.1 : Whether the Implementing Agency, NLDC, was carrying out calculations under the 2010 Sharing Regulations and the 2020 Sharing Regulations in contravention of the provisions of the said Regulations and various Orders issued by the Commission? Whether any directions required to be issued to Respondents 1 to 5 to recompute POC charges? Consequently whether Petitioners are entitled to any refund with interest?** **27.** We have considered the submissions of Petitioners and Respondents. Commission vide Interim Order dated 24.01.2022 in the instant Petition observed as follows: As per the above, the instant Petition was held maintainable to the extent of examining whether the transmission charges, as calculated by NLDC are in contravention of the provisions of the 2010 Sharing Regulations and Orders of the Commission. _Information provided by the DICs shall be vetted by the Implementing Agency as per the provisions of the Regulations and Detailed procedure notified by Implementing Agency._ **35.** Considering the above discussions, we are of the view that there is no double billing on the Petitioners and that the NLDC was carrying out calculations under 2010 Sharing Regulations and 2020 Sharing Regulations as per provisions of the said Regulations and various Orders issued by the Commission and hence no directions are required to be issued to Respondents 1 to 5 to recompute POC charges. All the prayers of the Petitioners are accordingly declined.
title: Petition under Section 79(1)(c) and (d) of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with Regulations 11(4) and other regulations of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Sharing of Inter-State Transmission Charges and Losses) Regulations, 2010 as amended by the third amendment effective from 1.4.2016 and orders, for direction in regard to the levy and collection of charges and losses from the Petitioners for the 500 kV Bipole Mundra-Mohindergarh HVDC Transmission Line along with its associated facilities. 1.
